messages.subject_clean: spatialShrunkenCentroids not clustering all available pixels?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am trying to cluster this obj:
mydata_peaks
An object of class 'MSContinuousImagingExperiment'
  <4369 feature, 28517 pixel> imaging dataset
    imageData(1): intensity
    featureData(0):
    pixelData(0):
    metadata(13): spectrum representation ibd binary type ... files name
    run(1): mydata_peaks_tic
    raster dimensions: 162 x 341 x 1
    coord(3): x = 1..162, y = 1..341, z = 0..0
    mass range:  100.0414 to 1349.5153
    centroided: TRUE

with the following line:
ssc <- spatialShrunkenCentroids(mydata_peaks,
                                   r = 1,
                                   s = 1,
                                   k = 2)

the clustering is successful but most of the pixels are not visualized in the groups - see attachment (I have tried with multiple r, s and k values but the number of assigned pixels doesnt change).

does anybody have a clue of what is going on here?

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
Your attached image seems to be an mz value, more than a cluster analysis.
I remember that in my old scripts and older versions of Cardinal this chunk of code worked for me:

#define custom colours for each cluster
mycol <- c(internal1="#FD9827", back="#42FD24", internal2="#1995FC", internal3="#FC23D9", internal4="#3524FB", internal5="#FC0D1B", backg="#CDFD34")

summaryPlots <- function(dataset, results, model, segment, name, col) {
  image(results, model=model, key=FALSE, column=segment, main=name, layout=c(3,2), col=col)
  plot(results, model=model, key=FALSE, column=segment, mode="centers", main="Shrunken mean spectrum", col=col)
  plot(results, model=model, key=FALSE, column=segment, mode="tstatistics", main="Shrunken t-statistics", col=col)
  top <- topLabels(results, n=9, model=model, filter=list(classes=segment))
  image(dataset, mz=top$mz, normalize.image="linear", contrast.enhance="histogram", smooth.image="gaussian")
}

###################################################
summaryPlots(sec, sec.sscg, model=list(r=1, s=3, k=8), segment=1, name="cluster 1", col=mycol)

Hope it helps you
